open_points.subject: disclosure-class ordering
open_points.text: “the members and the order have that one home” in `models`, but `canonical_values` also “Owns ... The order of disclosure classes”
open_points.question: Does `models` own the disclosure-class order while `canonical_values` merely consumes it, or does `canonical_values` own the order?
options: `models` owns members and order; `canonical_values` owns only the highest-class operation
`canonical_values` owns the order and `models` contains only the members
open_points.default_guess: `models` owns the enumeration and its order; `canonical_values` consumes that order to compute the highest class.

open_points.subject: equal content submissions under A01 rule 4
open_points.text: `canonical_values` “Owns A01 rules 1 and 4”, although rule 4 requires returning an existing stored record, preserving its first author and time, recording nothing, and not changing which version is current; `canonical_values` may know neither `store` nor the record-owning modules.
open_points.question: Which module owns the behavioural part of A01 rule 4 for each content-derived record?
options: each domain module owns idempotent submission for its records, using identities from `canonical_values` and atomic uniqueness from `store`
`store` owns all equal-record detection and the resulting current-version behaviour
`canonical_values` gains access to persistence and owns the complete rule
open_points.default_guess: Each record-owning domain module owns the equal-submission behaviour; `canonical_values` owns only canonicalization and identity computation, and `store` enforces atomic uniqueness.

open_points.subject: size validation against release ceilings
open_points.text: `data_provider` says “any check that uses a ceiling — each check belongs to the module whose rule it is”, while `canonical_values` says it owns value validation including “presence, carriage, schema, size”.
open_points.question: Who owns deciding and applying the applicable size ceiling when `fit_port_value` is used?
options: the calling domain module owns the size check and `canonical_values` checks only value shape and schema
`canonical_values` owns size checks using a caller-supplied ceiling
`canonical_values` selects and applies release ceilings itself
open_points.default_guess: The domain module selects and owns the applicable ceiling check; `canonical_values` provides schema and carriage validation plus a reusable byte-counting primitive.

open_points.subject: runtime validation of operation-node inputs
open_points.text: `runs` “Owns A12–A15”, including A13's validation of a value against a receiving node's input port, but its `Knows` list omits `bindings`; an operation `FlowNode` contains only `binding_id`, while the operation's input schemas and carriage are owned by `bindings`.
open_points.question: How does `runs` obtain the operation-port facts required to validate values entering an operation node?
options: add `bindings` to the modules `runs` knows and use `bindings.read_binding`
make `effects.reach_operation_element` own validation of operation-node inputs and its resulting `contract_violation` record
open_points.default_guess: Add `bindings` as a dependency of `runs` and read the accepted binding through `bindings.read_binding`; `runs` retains ownership of A13 receiving-port validation.
